$comment: Where the committed data came from, per tile and product. GeoSN rows were read from the portal's download-links service on the date in `retrieved` (see docs/data-pipeline.md#provenance for the query); `stand` is the provider's own currency field. Share tokens in the URLs are the portal's public folders and may rotate; the service is the durable index. OSM rows carry what the repository can prove; exact timestamps live in the raw files.

DGM1.$usedBy: markings.py and tram.py read only the DGM files' extents, to find a tile's neighbours (skyview.site_sources); skyview.py's horizon_<tile>.json carries the GeoSN credit

LSC.$comment: Laser-scan point cloud (LAZ): same flight as DGM1/DOM1 (Aktualität 2024-11-30 for 33412_5656 per the tile's _akt.csv — leaf-off). Used by the low-vegetation bake (pipeline/bake/lowveg.py; 0.5 m rasters under data/_raw/<site>/lsc/<tile>/, never committed): the measured height of the OSM hedges and the extra trees outside the canopy mask; and by the small-structure bake (pipeline/bake/small_buildings.py, plan 034, on the same rasters): the sheds, garden houses and container buildings LoD2 lacks, data/dlm/smallbuild_<tile>.geojson, baked on all fifteen tiles on 2026-09-26 from the LAZ files of 2026-09-25, and re-baked the same day reading 40 m of the neighbours' scan across each seam (a structure on a seam is kept once, by the tile holding its centroid), z the lowest ground under the whole rectangle (none where it falls > 1.5 m), overlaps > 0.5 m² resolved to the larger. The canopyx files were re-baked on 2026-09-26 too, against the trees files that by then carried the OSM trees (1 518 scan crowns a cadastre or OSM tree claims dropped). The flight (27-30 Nov 2024) caught the Christmas markets (the Striezelmarkt opened on 27 Nov): they are excluded through OSM pedestrian areas and squares. Baked for every tile. The spawn tile was baked first from a LAZ placed by hand; the other fourteen on 2026-09-25 by `bun run bake --ingest --lsc`. That day the download-links service still named the retired share rqcqdt8QMcLFUvC (503, Sabre NotFound); the current one, EpkzyJHScGb5ndd, is the `share_id` of LSC on the batch-download page, which ingest_sn.py now falls back to on its own.
LSC.committed: derived only: data/dlm/lowveg_<tile>.geojson, data/dlm/canopyx_<tile>.geojson, data/dlm/smallbuild_<tile>.geojson — every tile
LSC.raw: data/_raw/<site>/lsc/<tile>.laz, via pipeline/bake/ingest_sn.py --lsc (33412_5656 was baked from a LAZ placed by hand under data/_raw/lsc/lsc_<tile>_laz/)

LoD2.$comment: `stand` is the model's production year with the currency of its inputs in parentheses (laser scan for the roofs, Basis-DLM for the footprints, DGM for the ground); `creationDate` inside the CityJSON is the export date of each object. On 2026-09-25 the download-links service still listed the retired share GVzwbSyp7Yl7mBD (NotFound); the current one, AyJqXpJAZJXomCb, comes from the batch-download page (geodaten.sachsen.de/batch-download-4719.html, `share_id` of LoD2_CityGML). The eleven tiles added that day were converted with citygml4j 3.2.4 (the library citygml-tools wraps: CityJSON 2.0, 3 decimals); re-converting 33412_5656 that way reproduced the committed file object for object and vertex for vertex.

DOP_RGBI.$comment: `stand` is the flight date. 19 March 2024 is a leaf-off spring flight: deciduous crowns are bare, which is why the NDVI raster is low and median-centred and the crown colour remap recentres on that median.

Basis-DLM.$comment: One statewide package, replaced quarterly under the same URL, so the edition of a past download cannot be read from the portal afterwards. The derived files were baked from the package current in June 2026 (commits of 2026-06-12) and re-baked for rails and walls on 2026-09-18 and for rails, ballast and bridges again on 2026-09-24 (package downloaded that day); the package on the share was dated 2026-07-28 (Last-Modified, 1.23 GB) when this file was written. Record the package's Last-Modified and the metadata inside the ZIP at the next download.
Basis-DLM.schema: AAA-Anwendungsschema 7.1.2 (since 2025); Grundaktualisierung every 3–5 years, Spitzenaktualisierung of priority objects every 3, 6 or 12 months
Basis-DLM.editionInUse: land cover and veg rows: the quarterly package current in June 2026; rail, ballast, bridges: the package downloaded 2026-09-24 (exact release dates unrecorded), re-baked with it on 2026-09-26 for the measured bridges (ADR 0032); monuments: the package downloaded 2026-09-24 (the ZIP's inner package dated 2026-07-27, basisdlm_akt.csv 2026-07-28)

dresden.$comment: Landeshauptstadt Dresden open data, drawn by default (tree-inventory-layer.ts); also thins the laser-scan extra trees (pipeline/bake/lowveg.py). The WFS implements no paging and no count default, so one BBOX request per tile (+10 m) returns every tree; the ingest adapter (pipeline/bake/ingest_sn.py ingest_trees; extract-trees.sh when the committed files were baked) checks the feature count against the server's numberMatched (resultType=hits) and writes it, the request and the retrieval time to a .meta.json beside the raw cache. `aend_dat` in the raw file is each record's own last-change date (mostly 2025–2026).

Stadtbaumkataster.coverage: street trees, parks, schools and other municipal land; not the Großer Garten, not private ground
Stadtbaumkataster.retrieved: 2026-09-23 (the eleven tiles added on main: 2026-09-25; the four first tiles re-read 2026-09-25)
Stadtbaumkataster.raw: data/_raw/<site>/trees/<tile>.geojson (+ .meta.json); first baked from data/_raw/baumkataster/stadtbaum_<tile>.geojson, re-baked 2026-09-25 from the ingest adapter's cache (genus and trunk diameter `stammdurchmesser_akt` added)

numberMatched.$comment: per tile bbox incl. the 10 m margin; after the half-open tile clip: 3195, 3663, 6121, 5465 trees

wikidata.$comment: The bridges Wikidata places within 500 m of each tile (class, main span P2787, length P2043), fetched by the ingest (pipeline/bake/bridge.py fetch_wikidata) into data/_raw/<site>/wikidata/bridges_<tile>.json and matched to the decks by the rail bake; the matched item is the `wikidata` member of data/dlm/bridge_<tile>.geojson. Licence CC0, no credit required.
wikidata.dataAsOf: 2026-09-26 (the live database on the query day)

overpass.$comment: How the lamp, platform and bridge-structure files were fetched until 2026-09-24 (the bash bakes). Every OSM layer is now read from the Geofabrik extract below; kept for the history.

lowveg.dataAsOf: 2026-09-23 (timestamp_osm_base 16:16–16:20Z, data/_raw/osm/lowveg_<tile>.json; fetched from the maps.mail.ru Overpass mirror, overpass-api.de was overloaded)
usedBy: scripts/extract-lowveg.sh (the committed lowveg files; pipeline/bake/lowveg.py reads the local extract)

geofabrik.$comment: Regional extract read by pipeline/bake/osm.py (walls, lamps, platforms, bridge structure). `osmium fileinfo -e <file>` prints the extract's replication timestamp.

walls.query: barrier in (retaining_wall, city_wall, wall) or man_made=embankment
walls.dataAsOf: 2026-06-15 (re-baked 2026-09-24 by the Python pipeline; identical geometry. 2026-09-25: the two seam artefacts of the old polygon-first clip cut off — the 107.8 m on-edge segment along x = 412000 of wall #328 in 33410_5658 and #202 in 33412_5658 — exactly as the fixed bake cuts them; every other wall verbatim)

lamps.dataAsOf: 2026-06-15 (re-baked 2026-09-24 by the Python pipeline; the same lamps as the Overpass bake)

platforms.query: railway=platform, or public_transport=platform on a railway feature; each platform owned by the tile its centroid lies in

bbbike.$comment: City extract used where download.geofabrik.de is unreachable (it resets connections from the Claude Code cloud container; it was first used on 2026-09-24 for the fountains). Same OSM data and licence, cut to a bounding box (13.43–14.18 E, 50.88–51.23 N) that covers every Dresden tile; osm.py reads whichever .osm.pbf under osm/ is newest.

fountains.query: amenity=fountain (points and areas), with fountain=* and water=* for the basin style (data/dlm/monuments_<tile>.geojson)

bridges.query: man_made=bridge (bridge:structure, wikidata) and the inland-waterway marks seamark:type=bridge (seamark:bridge:clearance_height, wikidata); data/dlm/bridge_<tile>.geojson

platforms.query: railway=platform, or public_transport=platform on a railway feature (re-written by the rail step)

stairs.query: highway=steps (+ area:highway=steps outlines and barrier=wall/retaining_wall/city_wall for the width)

terraces.query: multipolygons on layer >= 1 (no building, man_made, landuse, bridge, railway or public_transport) that a flight the DGM runs flat under climbs onto

furniture.query: amenity in (bench, waste_basket, bicycle_parking, post_box), leisure=picnic_table, barrier=bollard (+ height, material), leisure=playground areas, playground=* equipment (points, ways, areas), highway=bus_stop / public_transport=platform with shelter=yes, amenity=shelter of shelter_type=public_transport; bench ways; every highway line for the bearing. Plan 030 (re-baked 2026-09-25, earlier objects unchanged): advertising=column (+ lit), highway=traffic_signals (+ traffic_signals:direction), emergency=fire_hydrant (+ fire_hydrant:type), amenity=clock (+ support, display), amenity=drinking_water, highway=bus_stop without a shelter; building outlines for wall clocks

surface.query: highway=* lines (surface, width, footway=sidewalk, sidewalk:*:surface, footway:surface) and highway/area:highway/amenity=parking multipolygons with a surface

sport.query: leisure in (pitch, track) multipolygons with sport=* and surface=* (nothing indoor, covered or on a roof), and leisure=track lines

fences.query: barrier in (fence, handrail) lines and area outer rings (fence_type, height); barrier in (gate, lift_gate, swing_gate, cycle_barrier) points within 0.5 m of a wall or fence line (width). Rings are clipped to the tile as lines (never the area as a polygon); a neighbour's gate whose gap reaches over the seam comes along as seam: true. Appended to data/dlm/walls_<tile>.geojson after its walls, which were kept from the Geofabrik bake of 2026-06-15. Trade-off: the older walls and the newer gates disagree in two places — two on: wall gates stood 70–73 m from any committed wall (33412_5656 at 412636.51, 5657834.37; 33412_5658 at 412288.74, 5658654.76); walls.py now keeps a gate only on a line its own file carries, and the two were dropped from the committed files on 2026-09-26 (a full walls re-bake from this extract would update the walls too and renumber them for scripts/terrain-study)
fences.dataAsOf: 2026-09-19 (first baked 2026-09-25; re-baked the same day with the seam fix)

osmBuildings.query: shop=* or amenity in (cafe, restaurant, bar, pub, fast_food, ice_cream, biergarten) points on the ground floor (no level, or a level list with 0) and building multipolygons carrying them; building multipolygons with heritage=*; joined to the LoD2 footprints (data/dlm/osmbuild_<tile>.json)

cultivated.query: landuse in (allotments, orchard, vineyard) and leisure=garden multipolygons, natural=tree points, highway lines (a colony's paths); the vine rows' slope from every committed DGM the vineyard touches; orchard trees less those a canopy, canopyx or trees point stands in for

markings.query: highway=crossing nodes (crossing, crossing:markings, crossing_ref), highway=traffic_signals nodes with traffic_signals:direction or direction, highway=* lines (lanes, oneway, lane_markings, cycleway, cycleway:right/left/both); measured on the class rasters of the tile and its neighbours, a neighbour's row reaching into the tile painted too

trees.query: natural=tree nodes (species/taxon/genus, genus:de/species:de, leaf_type/leaf_cycle, height, diameter_crown, circumference) more than 3 m from every cadastre tree; one with neither a taxon nor a leaf type is dropped
trees.dataAsOf: 2026-09-19 (first baked 2026-09-25 on the four first tiles: 1 820 trees; on all fifteen tiles 3 453 of the 10 854 natural=tree in the site, 8 292 of them classified, 298 with a genus)

riverside.query: man_made=pier (lines, buffered by width, and areas; floating=yes), man_made=groyne lines, route=ferry lines (name)

soundmarks.query: building=church|cathedral|chapel outlines, amenity=place_of_worship + religion=christian outlines, man_made=tower + tower:type=bell_tower and building=bell_tower; the tower's tip and height from the committed LoD2 and DGM1 of every tile (GeoSN, dl-de/by-2-0) — data/dlm/soundmarks_<tile>.geojson

smallBuildingsContext.query: the OSM context of the laser scan's small structures (see geosn.LSC): pedestrian areas and lines, place=square, amenity=marketplace, landuse=construction, amenity=parking (surface or untagged) — nothing kept there; building outlines confirm a vehicle-sized box

tram.query: railway=tram lines (bridge, layer); power=catenary_mast points within 15 m of a tram track; building outlines (the facades of the rosette spans); railway=tram_stop points and public_transport=platform / railway=platform (the stop signs, none by a shelter in the furniture of the tile or of its neighbours); all within 30 m of the tile
